page: Amazon Web Services r6i.large is an entry-level memory-optimized instance running on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. The system provides 2 vCPUs derived from 1 physical core with multithreading on an Intel Xeon 8375C processor running at a base clock speed of 3.5 GHz. The CPU cache architecture comprises 48 KB of L1 data cache, 1 MB of L2 cache, and 54 MB of L3 cache, alongside instruction set support for AVX-512, VAES, and SHA-NI. The instance is equipped with 16 GB of DDR4 memory operating at 3 GHz, offering 8 GB of RAM per vCPU. It does not include bundled local storage or dedicated hardware accelerators, and it operates with a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks reflect solid single-threaded execution constrained by the single-core physical topology. Single-core results are moderate, recording 1880.68 in stress-ng and 1589.0 in Geekbench. In contrast, multi-core performance falls into the lower percentiles with a Geekbench multi-core score of 1829.0 and a PassMark CPU score of 2962.06 due to the two-thread limit. Memory subsystem benchmarks show 103.16 GB/sec for small cached reads, tapering to 14.16 GB/sec for large uncached read transfers and 13.21 GB/sec for write operations. Synthetic operational benchmarks measured Redis SET operations at 1.95 million operations per second and static web throughput at 3.48 GB/sec.

The primary design tradeoff of the r6i.large is its compute-to-memory skew, delivering substantial memory capacity relative to processing capacity. This configuration provides qualitative cost efficiency for workloads that require moderate memory footprints without the expense of higher core counts. The absence of local disk drives requires reliance on network-attached storage volumes for state persistence. Workload profiles suitable for this server include small in-memory caches, development relational databases, message queues, lightweight enterprise application servers, and low-concurrency data ingestion pipelines.
description: Amazon Web Services r6i.large is a memory-optimized virtual machine built on the AWS Nitro System. Powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon 8375C processor clocked at 3.5 GHz, the instance provides 2 vCPUs across 1 physical core alongside 16 GB of DDR4 memory, yielding an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio. The architecture incorporates advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 and cryptographic accelerators, supported by 54 MB of L3 cache. Local storage is not included, requiring external network-attached volumes for disk access, while baseline network bandwidth is rated at 1 Gbps. Benchmark evaluations demonstrate solid single-thread performance paired with lower multi-core output and moderate memory transfer rates, directly reflecting the low core count. This instance offers a cost-effective operational footprint for memory-dependent tasks with modest compute requirements, such as small in-memory data stores, lightweight relational databases, and low-concurrency data processing pipelines.
